chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman praying in a shift and a khimār. He said: There should be over her a wrap which she draws closely around herself.

So the proper way to understand this report is that it indicates a kind of recommendation. It is also possible that what is meant is when the shift and the khimār are of the sort that do not conceal anything; for when that is so, a covering is unavoidable. And that which indicates what we have said is...

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman whose prayer attire is being discussed
key_terms.خِمَارٍ: a head covering worn by the woman
key_terms.دِرْعٍ: a body garment or shift worn by the woman
key_terms.مِلْحَفَةٌ: an outer wrap or covering drawn around the body

ai.seo_question: What should a woman wear for salat (prayer) according to this hadith from al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of a free woman’s dress in salat (prayer), stating that she should have an outer wrap over her garment and khimār. The concluding explanation clarifies that this may indicate recommendation, or that it becomes necessary when the clothing does not properly conceal the body.
